source.title: The neurology and evolution of humor, laughter, and smiling: the false alarm theory

confidence_rationale: The closest conceptual precedent for MECH-110: laughter follows an expectation (model) disrupted by an anomaly that turns out to be non-threatening, and the laugh signals a 'false alarm'. Tickling is framed as menacing approach followed by harmless contact, and pain-asymbolia patients (insular damage) giggle to pain -- danger sensed but no longer aversive. Mapping fidelity is high on the threat-then-safe logic, but this is a hypothesis paper in Medical Hypotheses with anecdotal clinical support and no data, so source quality is low.
failure_signatures: The false-alarm laugh is a single signal to conspecifics that an alarm was false; the paper does not propose that each exhalation pulse is its own threat-activation / resolution cycle.
The insular pain-asymbolia giggling is reported as clinical observation, not a controlled study, and could equally reflect disinhibition.
No temporal, respiratory or quantitative prediction is made or tested.

mapping.source_claim_statement: Laughter involves the build-up of an expectation followed by a sudden anomaly that changes the model -- but only if the new model is non-threatening; the loud laugh informs conspecifics of a 'false alarm'. Tickling (menacing approach, light contact) and insular pain-asymbolia giggling (pain sensed but not aversive) share this structure.
mapping.ree_translation: The anomaly corresponds to MECH-110's threat-hypothesis activation; the non-threatening new model is the safe-resolution step in which the sweep finds no genuine harm. The social 'false alarm' broadcast parallels MECH-110's V5-scoped social extension (group laughter as a joint 'threat absent' signal).
mapping.mapping_caveat: Ramachandran's unit is one false-alarm event producing one laugh signal; MECH-110's unit is each forced exhalation as a separate tag-clear cycle. The repeated-cycling mechanism and the plan-sweep-clock mapping are REE additions with no support here. Speculative hypothesis paper; clinical evidence is anecdotal.
mapping.source_context: Theoretical/evolutionary hypothesis paper drawing on primate threat displays, tickling, and neurological patients with insular lesions (pain asymbolia); no new data.

confidence_components.notes: Near-isomorphic conceptual precedent but data-free. Weighted toward source quality because MECH-110's missing piece is empirical, not conceptual.
